blocks.content: CoreDNS is the actual DNS server software modern Kubernetes clusters run to implement everything covered in the Cluster DNS topic, a flexible, plugin-based server, not a Kubernetes-specific invention.
1. The Real Server Behind Cluster DNS
blocks.text: 1. The Real Server Behind Cluster DNS

blocks.content: Where the previous topic covered the overall architecture, CoreDNS is the concrete software actually doing the work, answering every DNS lookup a Pod makes for a Service name.

blocks.alt: The real, concrete software actually answering every DNS lookup

blocks.content: CoreDNS is built around a plugin system, each plugin adds one specific capability, Kubernetes-aware service discovery, caching, logging, and more, chained together to define exactly how it handles incoming queries.

blocks.alt: A chain of small, focused plugins, each adding one specific capability

blocks.content: CoreDNS's behavior is defined by a configuration file called a Corefile, specifying which plugins are active and how they are configured, this is the file cluster administrators actually edit to customize DNS behavior.

blocks.alt: The actual configuration file controlling CoreDNS's real behavior

blocks.content: This is worth appreciating directly, CoreDNS itself runs as an ordinary Deployment and Service, exactly the same object types covered throughout this course, living in the kube-system namespace, it is not special, privileged infrastructure outside the normal Kubernetes model.

blocks.alt: An ordinary Deployment and Service, using the exact same objects as any other app

blocks.content: CoreDNS is not the original Kubernetes DNS implementation, an older component called kube-dns served this role previously, CoreDNS replaced it as the default in modern Kubernetes versions, offering a more flexible, extensible plugin architecture.

blocks.alt: The modern default, having replaced an older, less flexible implementation

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: CoreDNS is the actual, plugin-based DNS server modern Kubernetes clusters run, configured through a Corefile, to implement the cluster DNS architecture.
It runs as an ordinary Deployment and Service in kube-system, using the exact same objects covered throughout this course, and replaced the older kube-dns as the default.
